prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a climbing gym mat extending continuously from the camera wearer's foreground out to a background bouldering wall roughly 5 to 8 metres away, with five people arranged in a semi-circle 1 to 4.5 metres in front of the wearer. A person in grey trousers lies supine in the centre-foreground with their feet 0.8 to 1.2 metres from the camera wearer (within arm's reach in frame 2 where the wearer's brightly lit left hand reaches out at ~0.3 metres, partially occluding the person's right foot) and their head/hands holding a phone at ~2.5 metres, while two seated people to their left (in pink and black tops) and two seated people to their right (in grey and tan tops) sit roughly 0.5 to 1 metre apart at 2.5 to 4.5 metres distance, all facing away toward the upper wall and none looking at the camera wearer except the pink-shirted person who glances slightly sideways in frame 1. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's viewpoint pans slightly left and tilts upward while a standing person in black shorts approaches from the right edge—entering as a bright vertical silhouette at ~1.5 metres in frame 4 (partially out of view on the right) and stepping onto the mat to stand ~2.5 metres away on the right in frame 5, facing away toward the wall and within arm's reach (~1 metre) of the rightmost seated person. Compared to the RGB image, the depth map makes the continuous ground-plane distance gradient across the blue mat and the sharp depth separation between the approaching standing person and the seated group immediately clear. However, the map is unreliable beyond 5 metres, where the angled climbing wall, holds, and distant standing or seated background figures (at 6 to 8 metres on the far left and near the wall) flatten into uniform black with lost geometry.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground group on the mat into distinct `person` masks: the supine person in the centre (1 to 2.5 metres away, with feet cut off by the bottom frame edge in frames 3–5), the two seated people on the left (2.5 to 3.5 metres away, where the black-hoodie person partially occludes the pink-shirted person's right side), and the two seated people on the right (2.5 to 4 metres away, who shift from the right frame border into full view by frame 4 as the camera pans). It also segments the distant background figures on the far left in frames 1–3 (standing and seated on a bench 6 to 8 metres away, facing right) and a standing person near the base of the climbing wall (~5 to 6 metres away, facing toward the seated group and camera wearer), as well as the standing person in black shorts entering on the far right at 1.5 to 2.5 metres in frames 4–5 with their upper torso cropped by the top edge. Across the sequence, the map tracks the relative rightward shift of the distant left-side figures until they exit the left edge after frame 3, while the approaching right-side standing person moves into the space just right of the seated pair. This map makes it easier than in RGB to distinguish overlapping silhouettes—such as the standing climber at the wall behind the pink-shirted person in frames 4–5 and the closely seated pair on the right—as separate instances. However, it is highly unreliable in class labelling and completeness: the blue mat is only segmented as a `bed` in frames 1–2 and omitted thereafter, the camera wearer's own foreground hand in frame 2 is merged into the supine person's mask, the supine person's raised hands and phone are mislabelled as a `banana` in frame 3, and background wall features or people are intermittently misclassified as `tv`, `dog`, `sports ball`, or `car`.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the 5 frames, failing to detect skeletons for the supine person in front of the camera wearer, the seated group at 2.5 to 4.5 metres, and the standing person on the right at 1.5 to 2.5 metres. In frame 2, it renders a magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's own left hand raised at ~0.3 metres in the lower-left foreground (within reach of the supine person's right leg), and in frame 4 it reduces the supine person's raised hands holding a phone at ~2.5 metres to a small magenta cluster near the bottom-centre. Only the rightmost seated person in the tan shirt (~3.5 to 4 metres away, seated to the right of the grey-shirted person and facing away toward the climbing wall) receives yellow body keypoints in frames 3 and 5, showing their torso, head, and bent right arm/leg resting on the mat within ~0.5 metres of the grey-shirted person to their left and ~1 metre of the standing person to their right. What the pose map provides beyond the RGB alone is the precise finger-joint articulation of the camera wearer's egocentric hand in frame 2 and the limb angles of the rightmost seated person despite their turned-away posture. Overall, however, the map is severely unreliable due to extreme false negatives across nearly all visible people—likely caused by supine foreshortening, back-facing occlusions, and framing cutoffs—and noisy, collapsed torso keypoints on the single detected person in frames 3 and 5.
